instructions: Rinse the sprouts and pick out any that are brown or slimy. Mince the garlic and chop the green onions.
Put the sprouts and 6 tbsp of water in a medium pot with a tight lid. Cover and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes. Don't lift the lid.
Take the pot off the heat, lift the lid, and stir so the sprouts from the bottom move to the top. Let them sit for 30 seconds.
Drain the sprouts in a colander and let them cool for 2 or 3 minutes.

Transfer the sprouts to a large bowl. Add the garlic, green onions, 1 tbsp tamari, 1 1/2 tbsp sesame oil, 1 1/2 tbsp sesame seeds and a pinch of salt. Toss gently with your hands until everything is coated.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve at room temperature or cold.
To keep it, store it in an airtight container in the fridge for 4 to 5 days. Serve it cold; there's no need to reheat.
method_notes: Cup of Yum (4.9 from 27) is the lead: steam the sprouts in a covered pot with a little water, never lift the lid, then dress them while warm with garlic, green onion, sesame oil, seeds and soy. Beyond Kimchee has the same method with a 4 to 5 day fridge life. Amounts are scaled up to 1 lb, and tamari stands in for Korean soup soy sauce so the dish stays gluten-free; Takes Two Eggs and Kimchimari agree on the dressing and the rule not to overcook.
